correctness.rationale: The canonical-label and private-zero criterion is proved directly in both directions. Support of labels \(2\) lies in neither shore, one shore, or both. One-shore support preserves old minimal RDFs except isolated singleton defenders; mixed-shore support forces one defender in each shore and requires both to be nonuniversal. These disjoint cases give each term with correct exponent, including \(K_1\) boundaries. Direct exhaustive tests independently reconstructed graph joins and checked 281 pairs and 331245 assignments by single-coordinate decrements; tests corroborate rather than prove all orders.

value.rationale: The claim gives the complete two-variable distribution on a basic unrestricted graph operation from only factor enumerators and two elementary structural counts, including a nontrivial mixed-defender correction. Specializing to \(s=z=1\) gives an exact Roman census relation for all joins, and together with multiplicativity under disjoint union it computes all coefficients on cographs in polynomial time from a cotree. This addresses natural graph-composition and exact-enumeration questions rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
